sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Urbana?
sections.html:
In Urbana a seller has three options: an agent listing, a sale without an agent, or an as-is offer from a cash buyer. The city runs a rental registration program that matters if the house has tenants, and it sits beside one of the largest public universities in the country.

Urbana is in Champaign County, borders the city of Champaign, and holds most of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign campus. The Census Bureau counted 38,336 residents in 2020 and estimates 39,719 for July 1, 2025, a rise of 1.9% from the 2020 estimates base.

sections.h2: What do Urbana housing and households look like?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 describe a young, renter-heavy city with low home values compared with the Chicago suburbs.

  • Homes occupied by their owners: 37.3%
  • Typical value of an owner's home (median): $184,900
  • Median gross rent: $972
  • Households: 16,856, averaging 1.98 people
  • Median household income: $45,346; persons in poverty: 28.0%
  • Residents age 25 or older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 56.7%
  • Residents who had not moved in the past year: 72.8%
  • Average commute: 14.2 minutes

The 2020 census put the median age at 27.2, and the 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey counted 10,569 renter-occupied and 6,287 owner-occupied units.

sections.h2: Why are so many Urbana homes rentals, and how does the city regulate them?
sections.html:
The city says it has more than 10,000 rental units, nearly two-thirds of its housing, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign enrolls more than 50,000 students annually. The city adopted a Rental Registration and Inspection Program, described on its program page.

  • Every rental property must register each year and pay a fee from the city's schedule of fees.
  • The program year runs from October 15 to October 14, matching the leasing calendar.
  • It covers single-family homes, duplexes and multi-family buildings, including room rentals where the owner also lives there.
  • Nursing homes, hotels and motels, housing authority units and university-certified housing are excluded.
  • The city aims to inspect every rental on a cycle of three to five years, and results appear in its open data portal.

Registration happens online through a Citizenserve account. For questions, the Building Safety Division is at 217-384-2443. A seller who owns a rental should confirm the registration is current before listing and ask the division about the inspection record for the address.

sections.h2: Who collects the property tax on an Urbana house?
sections.html:
The Champaign County Treasurer and Collector bills and collects it, from the Bennett Administrative Center at 102 E. Main Street in Urbana, phone 217-384-3743. The county mails a single bill for the full year with coupons for two equal installments, and does not send a second bill. The collector handles more than 77,000 real estate bills for 156 taxing districts, which include school districts, cities and villages.

Champaign County real estate tax calendar for 2026 bills
DateWhat happens
May 1Bills are mailed
June 3First installment due
September 3Second installment due
September 30, 4:30 p.m.Last day to pay by check, e-check or card; later payments are cash, money order or cashier's check
October 1A $10 cost is added to each unpaid parcel for notices and publication
December 1 to 31Advance payments accepted, from 50% of the prior year's total up to 10% over it

The treasurer's pages state that postmarks do not apply to the late-payment dates. All of the 2026 dates above have passed, and the same pattern repeats with new dates each year. If the county does not have your current mailing address, call the Supervisor of Assessments at 217-384-3760.

sections.h2: What exemptions and tax programs can an Urbana owner use?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's tax page lists the programs and the office that handles each one. Most go through the County Assessment Office at 217-384-3760, which is also the number for corrections to bill information.

  • Owner-occupied exemption
  • Over-65 exemption for real estate, and the Senior Assessment Freeze
  • Disabled persons exemption and various veterans exemptions
  • Natural disaster homestead exemption
  • Tax deferral program for owners over 65, handled by the County Treasurer

Before you sell, ask the assessment office what is on file for the parcel, so the buyer's first bill is not a surprise. Champaign County has also elected to acquire delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts, beginning with the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 (Public Act 104-0553), so the county, as trustee for the taxing districts, takes the delinquent taxes at the sale in place of private tax buyers. A seller with back taxes should ask the Treasurer for a payoff before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: What shaped Urbana, and what do its neighborhoods offer?
sections.html:
Europeans first settled the area in 1822, calling it Big Grove. When Champaign County was organized in 1833 the county seat was set on 40 acres, and the name came from Urbana, Ohio. The Illinois Central line bypassed the town and ran two miles west, where West Urbana, later Champaign, grew around the depot.

The Urbana Free Library, founded in 1874, sits downtown. The Lincoln Square area hosts the Market at the Square each Saturday morning from May to November, running since 1979. East of downtown, the Candlestick Lane neighborhood, centered on Grant Place and parts of Fairlawn and Eastern Drives, lights its yards from the third Saturday in December through New Year's Day. Urbana uses a mayor-council form with seven wards.

The 1981 to 2010 NOAA normals list about 41 inches of precipitation and 23 inches of snow a year, with a July record high of 109 degrees and a January record low of minus 25.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and transit serve Urbana?
sections.html:
Urbana School District elementary schools are Leal, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Dr. Preston L. Williams Jr., Thomas Paine and Yankee Ridge, with an early childhood school on the Prairie Campus next to Williams. Urbana Middle School served 897 students in grades 6 to 8 as of 2024, and the current Urbana High School building dates to 1914. University Laboratory High School is a publicly funded lab school on campus and sits outside the district.

Most of the city lies south of I-74, with exits at Lincoln, Cunningham and University. University Avenue is US 150 and Vine Street and Cunningham Avenue carry US 45. Local buses run through the Champaign-Urbana Mass Transit District, and University of Illinois Willard Airport serves the area.

sections.h2: Do I have to disclose problems when selling an inherited Urbana house?
sections.html:
Not always. Illinois requires a seller of residential property to deliver a disclosure report before the contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20), but Section 15 exempts several kinds of seller, including a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, a transfer from a decedent by will or intestate succession, and transfers made under court order.

Whether an exemption applies depends on who signs the deed, so confirm that with the closing attorney. Ask the Champaign County Recorder for current deed recording requirements and fees before you schedule a signing.

faqs.q: Does Urbana require an inspection before I sell my house?
faqs.a: The city's permit and rental pages describe permits and a rental inspection cycle. Call the Building Safety Division at 217-384-2443 to ask whether anything applies to a sale at your address.

faqs.q: When are Urbana property taxes due?
faqs.a: Champaign County bills in two installments. For 2026 the installments were due June 3 and September 3, and the pattern repeats each year with bills mailed May 1.

faqs.q: My Urbana house is a rental. What should I do before listing?
faqs.a: Check that the rental registration is current, since the city's program year runs October 15 to October 14 and requires annual fees. Ask the Building Safety Division about inspection history, which also appears in the city's open data.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Urbana property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Champaign County Treasurer's Office, 102 E. Main Street in Urbana. A 24-hour drop box sits in front of the guard shack in the parking area, and cash, checks, money orders and cards are accepted, with cards and checks only through September 30.

faqs.q: How quickly can I sell a house in Urbana to a cash buyer?
faqs.a: As soon as the title work, payoff letters and deed are ready. A cash closing depends on the buyer's funds, the title company and the county's recording of the deed.
